source: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 20 · Publisher worked answer
label: JZ Mock E · Paper 2 · Question 20
knowledgePattern: Prove or refute triangle conditions using exact dissections and counterexamples
solution:
1 is true. For a right triangle, the altitude from the right-angle vertex to the hypotenuse gives two smaller triangles similar to the original by their angles. Conversely, a single straight cut producing two triangles runs from a vertex to the opposite side. The two angles at the meeting point on that side are supplementary. If both new triangles are similar to the original, those two angles are angles of the original triangle. They cannot be two different original angles, since two angles of a nondegenerate triangle sum to less than a straight angle. They must therefore be the same angle, and each must be a right angle.

2 is false. Let a triangle have area S, and choose r=(1+5)/2, so r2=r+1. A line from a vertex to the opposite side can divide the base, and hence the area, in the ratio 1:r. The two parts then have areas S/r2 and S/r, whose sum is S. These two areas and S form a nonconstant GP. This works for an equilateral triangle as well, so being right-angled is not necessary.

3 is true. In a kite, the diagonal through the two vertices where the equal adjacent sides meet perpendicularly bisects the other diagonal. One can derive this by splitting along the first diagonal, proving the resulting triangles congruent by SSS and comparing their angles. The four triangles made by the two diagonals therefore each have a right angle.

4 is false. The midpoint of a right triangle’s hypotenuse is the centre of its circumcircle, so the median from the right-angle vertex always has length half the hypotenuse. Thus it supplies no independent side-length information. For example, triangles with legs 2,2 and with legs 1,3 both have hypotenuse 2 and that median 1, but are not congruent.

5 is false. The converse fails for the rhombus A=(0,0), B=(2,0), C=(3,3) and D=(1,3). All four outside sides have length 2. Let M and N be the midpoints of AB and DC, and draw MN, AN and MC as shown.

The four triangles AMN, AND, MBC and MCN each have side lengths 1,2,7: the midpoint segments have length 1, the sloping parallelogram sides have length 2, and each long diagonal has length 22+(3)2=7. They are congruent by SSS and exactly tile the rhombus. They are not right-angled because 12+22≠7. Hence forming such a rhombus does not force P.

Exactly statements 1 and 3 are true. Answer F.

hints.title: Separate the directions of each claim
hints.body: For a necessary, sufficient or equivalent condition, write the required implication directions before working on the geometry.
hints.recap: Sufficiency tests condition implies target; necessity tests target implies condition; an equivalence requires both.
hints.pitfall: A construction for one direction does not prove its converse.
hints.pause: For each claim, decide what a proof must establish and what would be a valid counterexample.

recall.reminder: Sufficiency tests condition implies target; necessity tests target implies condition; an equivalence requires both.

hints.title: Track the angles where a cut meets a side
hints.body: For a single cut producing two triangles, consider the two angles created on the opposite side. Then use the angle correspondences required by similarity.
hints.recap: New learning: angles on a straight line sum to a straight angle, while the three interior triangle angles have the same total.
hints.pitfall: A similarity claim requires the whole angle pattern, not just one matching angle.
hints.pause: Determine which original angles can occur at the meeting point and complete both directions of the relevant claim.

recall.reminder: New learning: angles on a straight line sum to a straight angle, while the three interior triangle angles have the same total.

hints.title: Translate a shared-height cut into an area ratio
hints.body: A vertex-to-base cut creates two triangles with the same perpendicular height. Express their areas and the whole area in terms of a proposed geometric ratio.
hints.recap: Consecutive terms of a GP are related by one common multiplier.
hints.pitfall: The whole area is the sum of the two parts.
hints.pause: Check whether such a ratio requires any special angle in the original triangle.

recall.reminder: Consecutive terms of a GP are related by one common multiplier.

hints.title: Derive the kite angles from its equal sides
hints.body: Draw the diagonal joining the vertices at which the equal adjacent sides meet. Compare the triangles on its two sides.
hints.recap: New learning: three matching side pairs prove congruence; corresponding angles can then be compared.
hints.pitfall: Do not assume every diagonal property of a rhombus holds for every quadrilateral.
hints.pause: Use the equal angles and the intersection of the diagonals to assess the relevant claim.

recall.reminder: New learning: three matching side pairs prove congruence; corresponding angles can then be compared.

hints.title: Test uniqueness with distinct triangles
hints.body: Compare different right triangles with a common hypotenuse and locate the midpoint of that hypotenuse in their circumcircles.
hints.recap: The angle subtended by a diameter is a right angle; centre-to-circle distances are radii.
hints.pitfall: A length already determined by another datum may add no independent restriction.
hints.pause: Calculate the relevant medians and check whether the given lengths force congruence.

recall.reminder: The angle subtended by a diameter is a right angle; centre-to-circle distances are radii.

hints.title: Test the tiling converse by construction
hints.body: Try splitting a rhombus first into two congruent parallelograms, then split each along a matching diagonal.
hints.recap: A geometric counterexample must satisfy the construction exactly and fail the claimed angle or shape conclusion.
hints.pitfall: A sketch alone does not establish either congruence or a right angle.
hints.pause: Find exact side lengths for the resulting pieces, verify congruence and test whether they must be right-angled.

recall.reminder: A geometric counterexample must satisfy the construction exactly and fail the claimed angle or shape conclusion.
